lines: ſur certains faicts, & ouys autres teſ-
moins que ceux des enqueſtes faites par
le premier iuge. Mais quoy? ces enqueſtes
par authorité de la cour faites, les iuges
furent plus incertains que iamais: car de
vingt cinq ou trente teſmoins ouys d'of-
fice, les neuf ou dix aſſeuroyent que c'eſt
oit Martin Guerre: & ſept ou huit, que ce
eſtoit Arnauld de Tilb: & le reſte, pour le
conflict des circonſtances, & de la ſimili-
tude du priſonnier en doutoyent, n'o.
ſans aſſeurer que ce fuſt l'vn pluſtoſt que
l'autre.
Contemplent vn peu les iuges ici, & ſingulierement
les ſouuerains, combien il eſt dangereux, & plein de pe
rils, d'aſſeoir vn iugement, meſmes de l'honneur, & de
la vie, ſur le dire des teſmoins: leſquels, bien ſouuent
depoſent à credit: ou pour ſeruir à l'affectiõ de la partie
qui les produit, & miniſtre, plus qu'à la verité du nego-
ce: dont voyons ſouuentesfois aduenir, que ſur con-
traires faicts, diuerſes enqueſtes faites, reſultent preu-
ues repugnantes, ſeruant chacune à l'intention de ſon
maiſtre. Sur quoy faut bien que le iuge ſoit prudent, &
aduiſé: auquel la loy, par la bouche de Calliſtrat, remet
le tout diſant, TV DOIS, & peux mieux ſçauoir
quelle foy on doit adiouſter aux teſmoins, de q̃lle qua
lité, en quelle opinion ils ſont: & ſ'ils ont depoſé ſim-
plemẽt, ou choſes pourpẽſees, & tous d'vn meſme lan-
gage, & ſi ſur l'inſtant qu'ont eſté interroguez ils ont
chãcelé, ou reſpondu choſes vray-ſemblables {a}. Mais de
ces preuues par teſmoins, nous en dirons quelque mct
d'auantage ci bas, auec l'aide de Dieu {b}.

A point sort in the hyphen position, transcribed as printed.

uncertain.text: quelle foy on doit adiouſter aux teſmoins, de q̃lle qua
uncertain.note: 'q̃lle' is q + combining tilde (= quelle); the tilde is a flat stroke, not an acute

uncertain.text: ces preuues par teſmoins, nous en dirons quelque mct
uncertain.note: sic: 'mct' for 'mot' — the middle sort is an open c at 8x (right terminals, no closure), unlike the closed o's of 'dirons' on the line; wrong sort, kept as printed. A stray tick stands over the final t.

uncertain.text: d'auantage ci bas, auec l'aide de Dieu {b}.
uncertain.note: two points: (1) the print sets 'd'a uantage' with a gap, joined per §1; (2) after marker b a large round baseline dot with a much smaller wedge-shaped fleck just above it (8x); the page's colons have two equal round dots, so read as a period with a fleck. A colon with an under-inked upper dot cannot be wholly excluded.

printed tight as 'l.iij.P.ij.D.'; spaced per §1. The numeral between P. and D. shows at 10x as a single stem with two dots above and a j-curl at the foot: read as the italic 'ij' pair with its first stem unprinted (both readers 'ij'); 'j' alone is possible. 'P.' is presumably the paragraph sign printed as a P; as printed.

a small hook-shaped mark stands above the final o of 'anno' (margin-4.jpg); the word runs on to 'tation' on the next line, so it is neither a tilde nor, given its height and curve, the print's level break dash. Not transcribed. Reader A read it as a hyphen.
the numeral is printed with a lowercase l, two capital X and lowercase iij ('lXXiij' = 73); transcribed as printed

uncertain.text: ces preuues par teſmoins, nous en dirons quelque mot
uncertain.note: last word 'mot': at 12x (body-7.jpg) the middle letter is under-inked on its right side and at reading size can look like 'c' ('mct'); the bowl is round and o-wide, with faint ink at the top-right and bottom-right, so it is an 'o'. The final 't' is over-inked and carries the same stray tick as 'ſingulierement'. Read 'mot'.

decisions.reason: At 8x the middle sort is an open c: a bowl open on the right with a top and bottom terminal, the same shape as the c of 'ces' on the line; the o's of 'dirons' on the same line are fully closed and evenly inked. Wrong sort for 'mot', kept as printed (sic). The final t carries the stray tick B noted.

At 5x the mark is a small hook-shaped stroke rising above the final o, well above x-height and curving; this italic's line-end hyphen is a short level dash at mid-height (as in the p042 margin). It is a stray or accent-like mark, not a break sign; not transcribed, noted.
